## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The legacy fetcher's 8 attempts must come down to the project's 3-attempt retry cap before merge, because the only exemption it relies on is a sentence this pull request adds to the rules file. That exemption also sets no replacement limit and needs a bound or removal.

## Changes
Adds `app/legacy/fetch.py` (inventory fetch, 8 attempts, 10 s timeout) and `app/health.py` (health probe, 3 attempts, 2 s timeout), with parametrized tests for both in `tests/test_retries.py`. Adds a sentence to `docs/review-rules.md` exempting modules under `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap legacy fetch retries at 3 attempts — When the upstream is unreachable, `fetch_inventory` makes 8 attempts, breaking "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." (`docs/review-rules.md:5`, applied through `AGENTS.md:3`). The exemption at `docs/review-rules.md:7` is added by this pull request, so this review does not apply it. — During the nightly restart, one call can hold a worker thread for about 87 seconds when each attempt times out (8 × 10 s plus 7 × 1 s sleeps). — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS` to 3 or less and update the expected count at `tests/test_retries.py:10`, or have the rule's owners approve the exemption in a separate change first.

## Important
- docs/review-rules.md:7 — correctness — Retry-cap exemption for app/legacy/ sets no replacement limit — The added sentence lets any module under `app/legacy/` retry a network call any number of times. Line 6 gives the cap's reason as "Longer retry loops held worker threads for minutes when an upstream was down", which applies equally to a legacy upstream. — Once merged, later legacy modules with unbounded retry loops pass review, which is the failure the cap exists to prevent. — Fix: Remove the sentence, or replace it with a bounded limit for `app/legacy/` (attempts or total wall-clock time).

## Suggestions
- app/legacy/fetch.py:24 — correctness — Retry a connection dropped mid-body in fetch_inventory — A connection dropped after the headers but before the full `Content-Length` body arrives makes `resp.read()` (line 21) raise `http.client.IncompleteRead`, which is not an `OSError`, so `fetch_inventory` raises without retrying. The pull-request body gives dropped connections as the reason for the retries. — A nightly-restart drop during the body read fails the fetch on that attempt even though retries remain. — Fix: Catch `http.client.IncompleteRead` alongside `OSError` and extend `test_returns_body` with a `read()` that raises it.

## Not reviewed
- No CI or test-run result for `pr-71` was available; this review read `tests/test_retries.py` and did not run it.
